differences.title: 1. ACID Compliance
differences.leftDesc: Strict adherence to Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability for reliable transactions.
differences.rightDesc: Offers ACID compliance, but historically had some variations in strictness.

differences.title: 2. Data Types
differences.leftDesc: Extensive support for complex data types like JSONB, arrays, geometric types.
differences.rightDesc: Supports standard SQL data types, strong for traditional relational data.

differences.title: 3. Extensibility
differences.leftDesc: Supports custom functions, operators, data types, and procedural languages.
differences.rightDesc: Offers extensibility through stored procedures and triggers, but less flexible.

differences.title: 4. Concurrency Control
differences.leftDesc: Uses Multi-Version Concurrency Control for excellent read/write performance.
differences.rightDesc: Employs MVCC for efficient concurrent access to data.

differences.title: 5. Licensing
differences.leftDesc: Liberal PostgreSQL license, allows use in proprietary applications without strict obligations.
differences.rightDesc: GPL license requires modifications to be open-sourced, impacting some commercial uses.

differences.title: 6. Performance Tuning
differences.leftDesc: Offers many configuration options for fine-grained performance optimization.
differences.rightDesc: Well-optimized for common workloads, often faster out-of-the-box.

differences.title: 7. Community & Ecosystem
differences.leftDesc: Active, dedicated community with extensive documentation and extensions.
differences.rightDesc: Vast ecosystem, widely adopted, many tools and support options available.
